title: Chop, Chop, Timber
instructions: Swimmers curl into a ball on the pool edge as seeds. Pretend to water them and add sunshine; they grow into tall trees with arms raised. The instructor cuts down each tree in turn, cueing that swimmer to jump or fall into the water.

title: One-Two-Three, Go
instructions: Line swimmers up on the pool edge. They enter only when the caller uses the exact “One-Two-Three, Go” cue and stay put for any other phrase. The last correctly timed jumper wins. Leave enough space between participants to prevent collisions during entry.

title: Water Smart Game
instructions: With swimmers on the edge, describe water-related situations, such as swimming alone or swimming under lifeguard supervision. For a safe situation, swimmers jump in. For an unsafe situation, they remain on the edge and shake their heads.

title: What Time is it Mr. Shark?
instructions: Choose one participant as the shark at the opposite side of the pool. The other participants and instructor start together at an edge and ask the shark for the time. A numerical answer tells them how many steps to advance. At “lunchtime,” they return to touch their starting edge before being tagged. Tagged participants become sharks. The instructor may join the group but should avoid taking the shark role so they can continue watching everyone.

title: Front crawl: Torpedo kicking
instructions: Practise hip-led kicking while face down in a streamlined position. Increase the challenge with a less buoyant aid such as a floating brick or pull buoy. For more support, use a PFD, kickboard, shark fin, or noodle.

title: Front crawl: Side kicking
instructions: Lie on one side with the lower arm reaching past the head and the head resting on that shoulder. Look forward and kick quickly while keeping a taut, streamlined body. Practise on both sides to develop side breathing.

title: Front crawl: 6-kick switch
instructions: Start streamlined on one side and take 6 kicks. Use one stroke to roll onto the other side, take another 6 kicks, and repeat. Work on bilateral breathing, body roll, and a continuous kick.

title: Front crawl: 18 beaters
instructions: Start on one side with an arm extended overhead and take 6 kicks. Roll onto the front, extend both arms, and take 6 kicks. Use one underwater pull to turn onto the other side for 6 more kicks. Repeat, maintaining streamline in each position.

title: Front crawl: Resistance kicking
instructions: Kick in a streamlined position using a kickboard or the wall. For resistance, hold half the board below the surface while kicking.

title: Front crawl: Single-arm front crawl
instructions: Keep one arm reaching forward while the other performs long, controlled strokes. Choose enough buoyancy to let the swimmer concentrate on the arm action. A floating brick or pull buoy adds difficulty; a PFD, kickboard, or noodle provides more support.

title: Front crawl: Standing front crawl
instructions: Rehearse the arm action while standing on the deck or in shallow water. Focus on introducing the movement before adding swimming.

title: Front crawl: 3-stroke glide
instructions: Take 3 front crawl strokes. Pause on the third stroke to breathe, then continue the pattern to practise bilateral breathing.

title: Front crawl: Single-arm roll out
instructions: Begin face down in streamline. Pull one arm underwater past the hips while rolling onto the side. Breathe as that stroke finishes, then start recovering the arm. As the hand approaches the head, roll back onto the front and return the face to the water to exhale. Use technique appropriate to the swimmer’s level.

title: Front crawl: Elevator
instructions: Explore four head positions while swimming: fourth floor, chin at the surface; third floor, mouth in the water; second floor, nose in the water; first floor, correct swimming head position.

title: Front crawl: Head-up front crawl
instructions: Swim with the chin at the surface, looking at a fixed point on the far wall. Keep the kick close to the surface and the head steady instead of following the arms. This challenges the upper body.

title: Front crawl: Distance per stroke
instructions: Count strokes over a short distance, such as 25-50 m. Swim the same distance again and aim to use fewer strokes while maintaining effective technique.

title: Front crawl: Dry front crawl
instructions: Lie on one side on the deck. Reach the lower arm forward and rest the upper arm beside the body. Slide the upper hand toward the armpit with the elbow pointing upward. At the armpit, roll onto the stomach and continue reaching the hand past the head onto the deck.

title: Front crawl: Shark drill
instructions: Swim 3 strokes using high-elbow recovery. On the third stroke, breathe and pause with fingertips at the armpit for 3 seconds before continuing.

title: Front crawl: Thumb drill
instructions: Finish each underwater pull by touching the thumb to the hip, then begin the high-elbow recovery. Use the touch to reinforce a complete stroke finish.

title: Front crawl: Closed fists swimming
instructions: Swim front crawl with closed fists and high elbows. Concentrate on water pressure against the forearms, rather than relying only on the hands. The source identifies this as an advanced drill.

title: Front crawl: Finger drag
instructions: Keep fingertips trailing in the water throughout recovery. When the fingers reach the head, enter the whole hand and arm and extend forward. Maintain high elbows.

title: Front crawl: Zipper up/down
instructions: Kick on one side in streamline, holding an aid with the forward arm. Slowly slide the other hand from the leg to the armpit and back down. Work one arm at a time. Fins can reduce the kicking demand so attention stays on recovery and body position.

title: Back crawl: Kicking
instructions: Kick on the back using technique appropriate to the swimmer. Keep arms by the sides or stretch them overhead while holding a board. A less buoyant aid, such as a floating brick or pull buoy, increases the challenge.
equipment: Optional kickboard, floating brick, or pull buoy

title: Back crawl: Side kicking
instructions: Kick on one side with the lower arm extending beyond the head and the other arm beside the body. Focus on the kick and body roll.

title: Back crawl: Shake the shoe off
instructions: Sit on the pool edge and pretend to flick off a loose shoe or sock. Use small kicks and keep the knees down to encourage relaxed ankles.

title: Back crawl: Holy kicking
instructions: Kick on the back with elbows resting near the waist and hands raised together in a prayer position above the water. For more difficulty, slowly extend the arms upward, then lower them until the hands reach the stomach.

title: Back crawl: 6-kick switch
instructions: From a streamlined side position, take 6 kicks, use a stroke to roll to the opposite side, then take 6 more kicks. Repeat while keeping the head still.

title: Back crawl: Streamline kick
instructions: Kick on the back with both arms stretched beyond the head and pressed against the ears. Maintain streamline to work on kick strength and technique.

title: Back crawl: Fashion model
instructions: Place hands on hips while kicking on the back. Roll enough to lift one arm out of the water and take 6 kicks on that side. Roll to the other side and repeat.

title: Back crawl: 10-beat back crawl
instructions: Hold a streamlined side position for 10 kicks, then stroke with the forward arm to change sides. Keep the head steady throughout.

title: Back crawl: Single-arm back crawl
instructions: Swim using one arm while the other stays beside the body. As the stroking hand enters, roll the opposite shoulder out of the water. The resting arm may hold an aid for support.

title: Back crawl: Sky-bottom
instructions: Exaggerate the arm reach during back crawl: reach upward toward a noodle representing the sky, then downward toward the pool bottom.

title: Back crawl: Standing back crawl
instructions: Practise back crawl arms while standing on deck or in shallow water. For Swimmer 5 and above, use this to introduce the bent-arm pull.

title: Back crawl: Touch the rope
instructions: Provide a target about 3 feet above the water and have swimmers reach toward it on every recovery. Use a stretched rope or an instructor-held noodle, kickboard, or other object.

title: Back crawl: Transition back crawl
instructions: Take 3 right-arm strokes with the left arm at the side, then 3 left-arm strokes with the right at the side. Repeat with 2 strokes on each arm, then finish the length using full back crawl.

title: Back crawl: Sponge
instructions: Balance a sponge or another small object on the forehead while swimming. Keep it in place as the shoulders roll to practise steady head position.

title: Back crawl: Lane rope pull
instructions: Swim single-arm back crawl beside a lane rope, using the nearer arm and keeping the other at the side. Grasp the rope above the head, roll, and pull so the elbow bends underwater. Finish the pull beyond the hips.

title: Back crawl: Double-arm back crawl
instructions: While on the back, stroke with both arms together. Concentrate on the propulsive phase with bent arms.

title: Back crawl: Swim the rope
instructions: Use a rope across the pool or a lane rope as a pulling aid while swimming back crawl. Work the right arm in one direction and the left on the return, emphasizing the bend during the upsweep.

title: Back crawl: Distance per stroke
instructions: Count strokes over a chosen distance. Rest, then swim that distance again using fewer strokes to develop efficiency.

title: Back crawl: Closed fist
instructions: Swim with fists closed and concentrate on feeling the water and generating propulsion with the forearms.

title: Back crawl: Bounce
instructions: Hold a tennis ball in each hand while swimming. At the end of each stroke, release the ball past the hip as though pitching a fastball. Use this to emphasize the stroke finish.

title: Breaststroke: Vertical kicking
instructions: In a vertical position, extend each whip kick fully to lift the shoulders or chest above the surface.

title: Breaststroke: Vertical wall kicking
instructions: Face the pool wall with armpits supported at the gutter and stomach and upper legs against the wall. Practise whip kick while keeping the body close to the wall to emphasize lower-leg drive.

title: Breaststroke: Kicking with or without a board
instructions: Practise the kick on the front or back according to the swimmer’s level. Use a buoyant aid for support; remove the aid and keep streamline for a greater challenge.

title: Breaststroke: Penguin walk
instructions: Walk on deck or in shallow water with flexed ankles. Touch down on the heels only, keeping toes lifted and turned outward.

title: Breaststroke: Kicking off wall on land
instructions: Lie on the stomach on a wet deck with knees close to a wall. Flex the feet and press them into the wall to move the body forward. Focus on the part of the foot that should press against the water.

title: Breaststroke: Kicking on wall
instructions: Sit at the wall with legs bent 90 degrees. Begin with feet forward, draw heels toward the wall while keeping legs together, flex the ankles, then sweep the feet in a circle back to the start. Feel pressure along the inner feet and ankles.

title: Breaststroke: Ankle touch kicking
instructions: Keep arms beside the body. During kick recovery, bring the ankles to the hands to practise coordination.

title: Breaststroke: Streamline under
instructions: Kick underwater in streamline, return to the surface for a breath, then submerge again. Focus on breath control.

title: Breaststroke: Triple kick
instructions: Use 3 kicks for each arm pull, concentrating on body position and an efficient kick.

title: Breaststroke: Scull drill
instructions: Lie face down with arms extended past the head. Scull inward toward the centre line and outward again, keeping bent elbows near the surface and above the forearms. Vary wrist and elbow angles to find effective forward movement. Use a pull buoy to support the legs without kicking.

title: Breaststroke: Breaststroke arms on deck
instructions: Lie at the pool edge with shoulders and arms over the water in streamline. Pull the hands down and back toward the wall with elbows higher than hands. Bring hands and elbows together at the centre, then extend them forward.

title: Breaststroke: Arms only
instructions: Place a noodle under the armpits for support. Flutter kick while practising breaststroke arms, using the noodle as the limit behind which the arms should not travel.

title: Breaststroke: Coordination pattern
instructions: Stand in shallow water or lie over the pool edge. Rehearse the pull, breath, and kick sequence, with instructor assistance where needed.

title: Breaststroke: Head-up breaststroke
instructions: Swim full breaststroke with the head lifted and eyes looking forward. Concentrate on the arm pull and leg kick without adding underwater breathing.

title: Breaststroke: Shooters
instructions: Begin the pull slowly and feel the hands and arms working against the water. As the hands meet at the centre of the body, drive the arms forward quickly to practise fast recovery.

title: Dry land: Chest stretch
instructions:
Stand upright with feet a little wider than the shoulders. Extend straight arms sideways at shoulder height with palms facing forward. Move the arms back and hold.

Source coaching notes: move slowly, relax, keep breathing, and avoid stretching beyond mild discomfort. Hold static positions for at least 15 seconds unless the exercise gives a different hold time.

title: Dry land: Side bends
instructions:

title: Dry land: Abdominal and lower back muscles
instructions:
Lie face down with arms extended forward. Lift the hands, chest, and shoulders so the toes and torso remain on the ground. The stretch is felt through the back and abdomen.

title: Dry land: Gluteus muscles
instructions:
Lie face down. Gently contract the buttocks for 10 seconds, then relax. Lift and extend one arm for 10 seconds, then the other. Repeat with each leg. Next lift the right arm with the left leg for 10 seconds, then swap diagonals.

Source coaching notes: move slowly, relax, keep breathing, and avoid stretching beyond mild discomfort. Hold static positions for at least 15 seconds unless the exercise gives a different hold time.

title: Dry land: Swimming (dry land)
instructions:
Lie face down and lift arms and legs off the ground. Flutter both arms and legs together to imitate swimming.

title: Dry land: Calf stretch
instructions:
Face a wall with hands on it and arms straight. Step one leg farther back. Put the toes of the nearer foot against the wall while keeping its heel on the floor. Bend the elbows, lean toward the wall, and hold. Change feet.

Source coaching notes: move slowly, relax, keep breathing, and avoid stretching beyond mild discomfort. Hold static positions for at least 15 seconds unless the exercise gives a different hold time.

title: Dry land: Arm swings and hand claps
instructions:
Circle one arm 10 times, repeat with the other, then circle both together. Next extend arms forward, open them backward, and bring them forward to clap. Repeat the clap movement 10 times.

Source coaching notes: move slowly, relax, keep breathing, and avoid stretching beyond mild discomfort. Hold static positions for at least 15 seconds unless the exercise gives a different hold time.

title: Dry land: Lunges
instructions:
Walk forward using a lunge on each step. Keep hips facing forward and direct the pressure through the heel rather than the toes.

Source coaching notes: move slowly, relax, keep breathing, and avoid stretching beyond mild discomfort. Hold static positions for at least 15 seconds unless the exercise gives a different hold time.

title: Dry land: Jump starts
instructions:
Bring heels together with toes turned out. Squat with heels between the legs, then jump upward and reach overhead. Repeat.

title: Sample warm-up
instructions:
200 m mixed strokes at an easy pace, changing stroke every 25 or 50 m.
4 × 50 m varying the time: begin relaxed, then slightly faster, then strong effort, then fast.
Pace progression shown in the source: 25 m relaxed; 50 m slightly faster; 75 m strong effort; 100 m fast.

This is a warm-up component, not a complete workout.

title: 11 years & under: Main set A
instructions:
4 × 25 m front crawl; start every 1:00.
2 × 25 m flutter kick with a board; rest 20 seconds after each repeat.
2 × 25 m flutter kick without a board; rest 20 seconds after each repeat.
4 × 25 m, starting every 1:00: closed-fist front crawl on odd lengths, distance-per-stroke focus on even lengths.

DPS means distance per stroke: cover the distance efficiently with fewer strokes. Add an appropriate warm-up and cool-down.

title: 11 years & under: Main set B
instructions:
2 × 50 m front crawl; start every 1:40.
Then a distance ladder: 25 m, 50 m, 75 m, 75 m, 50 m, 25 m. The source does not specify a stroke or interval for the ladder.

Add an appropriate warm-up and cool-down.

title: 11-14 years: Main set A
instructions:
4 × 75 m front crawl; start every 2:00.
3 × 50 m front crawl; start every 1:20.
2 × 25 m front crawl; start every 55 seconds.

Add an appropriate warm-up and cool-down.

title: 11-14 years: Main set B
instructions:
8 × 25 m, alternating breaststroke on odd lengths and back crawl on even lengths.
2 × 75 m, each consisting of 25 m back flutter kick and 50 m back crawl.
2 × 75 m, each consisting of 25 m whip kick without a board and 50 m breaststroke.

The source does not give rest intervals. Add an appropriate warm-up and cool-down.

title: 13-18 years: Main set A
instructions:
3 × 100 m front crawl; start every 2:45.
2 × 100 m front crawl; start every 2:35.
1 × 100 m front crawl sprint.

Add an appropriate warm-up and cool-down.

title: 13-18 years: Main set B
instructions:
Pyramid:
25 m front crawl; rest 20 seconds.
50 m back crawl; rest 30 seconds.
75 m breaststroke; rest 45 seconds.
100 m front crawl; rest 1 minute.
75 m breaststroke; rest 45 seconds.
50 m back crawl; rest 30 seconds.
25 m front crawl; rest 20 seconds.

Add an appropriate warm-up and cool-down.

title: Sample cool-down
instructions:
200 m easy mixed strokes, changing stroke every 25 or 50 m.
4 × 50 m easy swimming, stroke of choice, with a distance-per-stroke focus.
6 × 25 m, stroke of choice, with 25 seconds of rest after each repeat.

DPS means distance per stroke. This is a cool-down component, not a complete workout.

title: 11 years & under: Interval workout 1
instructions:
Warm-up
1 × 25 m, 1 × 50 m, then 1 × 75 m; stroke of choice with 20 seconds of rest after each swim.

Main set
2 × 25 m flutter kick; start every 1:10.
2 × 25 m front crawl; start every 1:00.
2 × 50 m, stroke of choice; start every 2:00.

Cool-down
1 × 25 m, 1 × 50 m, then 1 × 75 m; stroke of choice with 20 seconds of rest after each swim.

title: 11 years & under: Interval workout 2
instructions:
Warm-up
4 × 25 m, stroke of choice; start every 1:00.

Main set
8 × 25 m front crawl; start every 55 seconds.

Cool-down
4 × 25 m, stroke of choice; start every 1:00.

title: 11-14 years: Interval workout 1
instructions:
Warm-up
4 × 25 m, stroke of choice; start every 1:00.

Main set
25 m, stroke of choice; rest 15 seconds.
50 m, stroke of choice; rest 30 seconds.
50 m, stroke of choice; rest 30 seconds.
25 m, stroke of choice; rest 15 seconds.

Cool-down
4 × 25 m, stroke of choice; start every 1:00.

title: 11-14 years: Interval workout 2
instructions:
Warm-up
100 m, stroke of choice.

Main set
6 × 50 m front crawl; start every 1:30.
2 × 25 m flutter kick without a board, arms streamlined; rest 20 seconds after each repeat.
2 × 25 m 6-kick switch side glides; rest 20 seconds after each repeat.

Cool-down
100 m, stroke of choice.

title: 13-18 years: Interval workout 1
instructions:
Warm-up
2 × 25 m, stroke of choice; rest 20 seconds after each repeat.
2 × 50 m, stroke of choice; rest 30 seconds after each repeat.

Main set
12 × 25 m, stroke of choice at a hard effort; start every 1:00.
4 × 50 m, stroke of choice at a hard effort; start every 1:30.
